10	
11	This repo runs Vitest 4.1, which ignores `vitest.workspace.ts`. Every test runs under the root `vitest.config.mts`, whose only setup file is `packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts`. That file provides the jest-dom matchers and a ResizeObserver polyfill. The per-project setups named in the workspace file, such as `packages/ui/components/test-setup.tsx` with its next/navigation, useLocale and useIsPlatform mocks, never run.
12	
13	**Why:** anything that renders `@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog` throws "invariant expected app router to be mounted" unless the test file mocks `next/navigation`'s `useRouter` itself. `EditLocationDialog.test.tsx` and `RescheduleDialog.test.tsx` both do this.
14	
15	**How to apply:**
16	- When writing an `apps/web` component test, mock `next/navigation` (`useRouter`) and `@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale` in the test file.
17	- Run a single file with `yarn test <path>`. The script sets TZ=UTC, so the command also works in PowerShell.
18	- To type-check one test file with a temporary tsconfig placed outside the repo, set `typeRoots` to the repo's `node_modules/@types`. Otherwise `@types/jest` and `@types/testing-library__jest-dom` go missing and you get false errors.
19	
20	Type checking on Julissa's Windows machine:
21	- `yarn type-check:ci --force` fails there with `spawn tsc ENOENT`. The `tsc-absolute` wrapper can't launch tsc on Windows, so this is a tooling problem, not a code problem.
22	- That run also re-formats `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` to LF line endings, a change with no content difference. Undo it with `git restore`.
23	- Instead, type-check the web app with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false -p apps/web/tsconfig.json` (~72s, the same heap CI uses).
24	
25	Local database facts, verified 2026-10-29:
26	- Julissa's dev DB runs in docker container `prisma-postgres-1` (postgres:18) and is reached at `localhost:5450/calendso` via `.env`. `packages/prisma/.env` is a symlink to the root `.env`.
27	- Running the Prisma CLI from the repo root fails with "conflict between env vars in .env and packages\prisma\.env", so run it from `packages/prisma`.
28	- An inline `DATABASE_URL`/`DATABASE_DIRECT_URL` overrides `.env`. `migrate status` prints a `Datasource … at host:port` line, which is the safe pre-flight check.
29	- `@calcom/prisma`'s `build` script (`auto-migrations.ts`) runs `migrate deploy` against the `.env` DB unless `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1`. So `yarn build` migrates the dev DB. `type-check:ci` only runs post-install, so it doesn't.
30	- Avoid `db-migrate` (migrate dev), `db-reset`, `db-nuke` and `dx` against the dev DB.
31
```

10	
11	Code-traced on 2026-10-29, not reproduced on a running instance — re-verify before citing:
12	
13	- `validateRole` in `authorizeCredentials` (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`) downgrades password-login admins lacking 2FA or a 15+ char password to `INACTIVE_ADMIN`, but only in the JWT / client session (hides Admin tab, shows `AdminPasswordBanner`). Server checks read `role` from the DB: custom `getServerSession` (`role: user.role`), tRPC `isAdminMiddleware` via `findUnlockedUserForSession`, API v2 `isSystemAdmin`. So those admins still pass admin pages and admin tRPC (incl. `toggleFeatureFlag`) via direct URL/API.
14	- `validateRole` is skipped when `NODE_ENV=development` (`yarn dev`), when `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E` is set, and for Google/Azure admins — so the team likely never sees it locally.
15	- Custom `getServerSession` keeps only a few token fields (belongsToActiveTeam, org, orgAwareUsername, profileId, upId), and the jwt `trigger === "update"` branch ignores custom fields. A flag stored in the session at login reaches `useSession()` but not server code.
16	- The TOTP `setup` route requires a password, so Google/Azure-only users can't enroll in 2FA.
17	- tRPC `ctx.user` already carries DB-fresh `role`, `twoFactorEnabled`, `identityProvider`, so per-request admin gating needs only a flag lookup.
18	- `admin/users/[id]/edit/page.tsx` loads another user's record server-side with only the admin `layout.tsx` guarding it (repo rule wants page-level checks).
19	- #111's `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide()` had no enforcement callers yet.
20	- Pre-existing gaps to file separately: email magic-link sign-in never asks for TOTP; `viewer.users.list`/`get` return full user rows incl. encrypted `twoFactorSecret`/`backupCodes`; the INACTIVE_ADMIN weak-password case isn't enforced server-side.
21	
22	**Why:** these drove #67's requirement for server-side, per-request admin checks ([[issue-67-admin-2fa]]).
23	**How to apply:** treat as leads, not facts — re-check the code (it may change once #112 lands) before stating any of this to Julissa or the team.

A user who logs in with a password and doesn't have 2FA sees a setup window that can't be closed. They go through the existing setup steps: confirm their password, scan the QR code, enter the 6-digit code and save their backup codes. Then they use the app normally. A new user who signs up with email and password has to complete a 2FA step during onboarding. Users who sign in with Google or another provider aren't affected. When the setting is off, nothing changes.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. At login, the server decides whether the user must set up 2FA and stores the result in their session. All three conditions must hold: the setting is on, the user doesn't have 2FA, and the user signs in with a password. The browser can't skip this check.\n\n2. While setup is required, a 2FA setup window appears on every page. It reuses the existing setup steps and has no Cancel or Close button.\n\n3. After finishing setup, the user can use the app normally.\n\n4. When the setting is on, onboarding includes a required 2FA step for users who sign up with a password. Otherwise the step is skipped.\n\n5. Users who sign in through Google or another identity provider are exempt, since they can't set up 2FA in cal.diy.\n\n6. Write tests for the login rule, covering each of the three conditions, and for the onboarding step.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n* Storing or toggling the setting (sub-issue 1)\n* Forcing setup on users who were already logged in when the setting was turned on. The rule applies at their next login.\n* A per-team version of the setting\n* Changes to how 2FA itself works","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOTleCnc8AAAABgG8iMA","author":{"login":"kojoshuay"},"authorAssociation":"COLLABORATOR","body":"spec looks good!","createdAt":"2026-10-27T18:01:31Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/issues/112#issuecomment-6449734192","viewerDidAuthor":false}],"labels":[],"number":112,"state":"OPEN","title":"Require users to set up 2FA when the admin setting is on"}

14980	diff --git a/apps/web/modules/auth/components/RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx b/apps/web/modules/auth/components/RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx
14981	new file mode 100644
14982	index 0000000000..65c495e137
14983	--- /dev/null
14984	+++ b/apps/web/modules/auth/components/RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx
14985	@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
14986	+"use client";
14987	+
14988	+import { trpc } from "@calcom/trpc/react";
14989	+import EnableTwoFactorModal from "@calcom/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal";
14990	+import { signOut, useSession } from "next-auth/react";
14991	+import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
14992	+
14993	+export function RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal() {
14994	+  const utils = trpc.useUtils();
14995	+  const { data: session, update } = useSession();
14996	+  const isRequired = session?.user.requiresTwoFactorSetup === true;
14997	+
14998	+  // Stays open once opened, because 2FA is enabled before the backup codes step. A session refetch
14999	+  // at that point (e.g. on window focus) clears the flag, which would otherwise hide the codes.
15000	+  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
15001	+
15002	+  useEffect(() => {
15003	+    if (isRequired) setOpen(true);
15004	+  }, [isRequired]);
15005	+
15006	+  if (!open) return null;
15007	+
15008	+  const handleEnable = async () => {
15009	+    if (session?.user.role === "INACTIVE_ADMIN") {
15010	+      // Session role is set at login time, so admins need to sign in again to restore it
15011	+      signOut({ callbackUrl: "/auth/login" });
15012	+      return;
15013	+    }
15014	+    await update();
15015	+    setOpen(false);
15016	+    utils.viewer.me.invalidate();
15017	+  };
15018	+
15019	+  return <EnableTwoFactorModal open isRequired onEnable={handleEnable} />;
15020	+}

15181	+import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
15182	+import { useSession } from "next-auth/react";
15183	+import { useSubmitPersonalOnboarding } from "./useSubmitPersonalOnboarding";
15184	+
15185	+export const PERSONAL_TWO_FACTOR_STEP_PATH = "/onboarding/personal/two-factor";
15186	+
15187	+export const getPersonalOnboardingTotalSteps = (requiresTwoFactorSetup: boolean) =>
15188	+  requiresTwoFactorSetup ? 3 : 2;
15189	+
15190	+export const useFinishPersonalOnboarding = () => {
15191	+  const router = useRouter();
15192	+  const { data: session } = useSession();
15193	+  const { submitPersonalOnboarding, isSubmitting } = useSubmitPersonalOnboarding();
15194	+  const requiresTwoFactorSetup = session?.user.requiresTwoFactorSetup === true;
15195	+
15196	+  const finishPersonalOnboarding = () => {
15197	+    // Onboarding is only marked complete after the 2FA step, so it can't be finished without 2FA
15198	+    if (requiresTwoFactorSetup) {
15199	+      router.push(PERSONAL_TWO_FACTOR_STEP_PATH);
15200	+      return;
15201	+    }
15202	+    submitPersonalOnboarding();
15203	+  };
15204	+
15205	+  return {
15206	+    finishPersonalOnboarding,
15207	+    isSubmitting,
15208	+    totalSteps: getPersonalOnboardingTotalSteps(requiresTwoFactorSetup),
15209	+  };
15210	+};

15856	+export async function requiresTwoFactorSetup(user: {
15857	+  identityProvider: IdentityProvider;
15858	+  twoFactorEnabled: boolean;
15859	+}): Promise<boolean> {
15860	+  // Users of external identity providers can't set up 2FA in Cal.diy, so they are exempt
15861	+  if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL || user.twoFactorEnabled) return false;
15862	+
15863	+  // Runs on every session fetch, so it reads the cached flag. Toggling the flag clears that cache entry.
15864	+  return getFeatureRepository().checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally(REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH_FLAG);
15865	+}

import { defaultResponderForAppDir } from "app/api/defaultResponderForAppDir";
import { parseRequestData } from "app/api/parseRequestData";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { cookies, headers } from "next/headers";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { authenticator } from "otplib";
import qrcode from "qrcode";

import { ErrorCode } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/ErrorCode";
import { getServerSession } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/getServerSession";
import { verifyPassword } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/verifyPassword";
import { checkRateLimitAndThrowError } from "@calcom/lib/checkRateLimitAndThrowError";
import { symmetricEncrypt } from "@calcom/lib/crypto";
import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
import { IdentityProvider } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

import { buildLegacyRequest } from "@lib/buildLegacyCtx";

async function postHandler(req: NextRequest) {
  const body = await parseRequestData(req);
  const session = await getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) });

  if (!session) {
    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  if (!session.user?.id) {
    console.error("Session is missing a user id.");
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
  }

  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
    rateLimitingType: "core",
    identifier: `api:totp-setup:${session.user.id}`,
  });

  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: session.user.id }, include: { password: true } });

  if (!user) {
    console.error(`Session references user that no longer exists.`);
    return NextResponse.json({ message: "Not authenticated" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !user.password?.hash) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled }, { status: 400 });
  }

  if (!user.password?.hash) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.UserMissingPassword }, { status: 400 });
  }

  if (user.twoFactorEnabled) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled }, { status: 400 });
  }

  if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) {
    console.error("Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with two factor setup.");
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError }, { status: 500 });
  }

  const isCorrectPassword = await verifyPassword(body.password, user.password.hash);
  if (!isCorrectPassword) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: ErrorCode.IncorrectPassword }, { status: 400 });
  }

  // This generates a secret 32 characters in length. Do not modify the number of
  // bytes without updating the sanity checks in the enable and login endpoints.
  const secret = authenticator.generateSecret(20);

  // Generate backup codes with 10 character length
  const backupCodes = Array.from(Array(10), () => crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"));

  await prisma.user.update({
    where: {
      id: session.user.id,
    },
    data: {
      backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
      twoFactorEnabled: false,
      twoFactorSecret: symmetricEncrypt(secret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY),
    },
  });

  const name = user.email || user.username || user.id.toString();
  const keyUri = authenticator.keyuri(name, "Cal", secret);
  const dataUri = await qrcode.toDataURL(keyUri);

  return NextResponse.json({ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes });
}

export const POST = defaultResponderForAppDir(postHandler);

async function sendVerificationLogin(email: string, username: string, t: (key: string) => string) {
  await signIn("email", {
    email: email.toLowerCase(),
    username: username.toLowerCase(),
    redirect: false,
    callbackUrl: WEBAPP_URL || "https://app.cal.com",
  })
    .then(() => {
      showToast(t("verification_email_sent"), "success");
    })
    .catch((err) => {
      showToast(err, "error");
    });
}

function useSendFirstVerificationLogin({
  email,
  username,
}: {
  email: string | undefined;
  username: string | undefined;
}) {
  const sent = useRef(false);
  const { t } = useLocale();
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!email || !username || sent.current) {
      return;
    }
    (async () => {
      await sendVerificationLogin(email, username, t);
      sent.current = true;
    })();
  }, [email, username, t]);
}

const querySchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().optional(),
  username: z.string().optional(),
  paymentStatus: z.string().optional(),
  t: z.string().optional(),
});

const PaymentFailedIcon = () => (
  <div className="rounded-full bg-orange-900 p-3">
    <TriangleAlertIcon className="h-6 w-6 shrink-0 p-0.5 font-extralight text-orange-100" />

);

    37	 * frequently enough on the client-side to keep the session alive.

    41	  authOptions?: AuthOptions;
    42	}) {
    43	  const { req, authOptions: { secret } = {} } = options;

     1	import * as DialogPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-dialog";
     2	import { usePathname, useRouter } from "next/navigation";
     3	import { useState } from "react";
     4	
     5	import { useIsPlatform } from "@calcom/atoms/hooks/useIsPlatform";
     6	import { useCompatSearchParams } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useCompatSearchParams";
     7	import { Dialog as BaseDialog } from "@calcom/ui/components/dialog";
     8	
     9	export type DialogProps = React.ComponentProps<(typeof DialogPrimitive)["Root"]> & {
    10	  name?: string;
    11	  clearQueryParamsOnClose?: string[];
    12	};
    13	
    14	const enum DIALOG_STATE {
    15	  // Dialog is there in the DOM but not visible.
    16	  CLOSED = "CLOSED",
    17	  // State from the time b/w the Dialog is dismissed and the time the "dialog" query param is removed from the URL.
    18	  CLOSING = "CLOSING",
    19	  // Dialog is visible.
    20	  OPEN = "OPEN",
    21	}
    22	
    23	export function Dialog(props: DialogProps) {
    24	  const isPlatform = useIsPlatform();
    25	  return !isPlatform ? <ControlledDialog {...props} /> : <DialogPrimitive.Dialog {...props} />;
    26	}
    27	
    28	function ControlledDialog(props: DialogProps) {
    29	  const router = useRouter();
    30	  const pathname = usePathname();
    31	  const searchParams = useCompatSearchParams();
    32	  const newSearchParams = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString());
    33	  const { children, name, ...dialogProps } = props;
    34	
    35	  // only used if name is set
    36	  const [dialogState, setDialogState] = useState(dialogProps.open ? DIALOG_STATE.OPEN : DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED);
    37	  const shouldOpenDialog = newSearchParams.get("dialog") === name;
    38	  if (name) {
    39	    const clearQueryParamsOnClose = ["dialog", ...(props.clearQueryParamsOnClose || [])];
    40	    dialogProps.onOpenChange = (open) => {
    41	      if (props.onOpenChange) {
    42	        props.onOpenChange(open);
    43	      }
    44	
    45	      // toggles "dialog" query param
    46	      if (open) {
    47	        newSearchParams.set("dialog", name);
    48	      } else {
    49	        clearQueryParamsOnClose.forEach((queryParam) => {
    50	          newSearchParams.delete(queryParam);
    51	        });
    52	        router.push(`${pathname}?${newSearchParams.toString()}`);
    53	      }
    54	      setDialogState(open ? DIALOG_STATE.OPEN : DIALOG_STATE.CLOSING);
    55	    };
    56	
    57	    if (dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED && shouldOpenDialog) {
    58	      setDialogState(DIALOG_STATE.OPEN);
    59	    }
    60	
    61	    if (dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.CLOSING && !shouldOpenDialog) {
    62	      setDialogState(DIALOG_STATE.CLOSED);
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    // allow overriding
    66	    if (!("open" in dialogProps)) {
    67	      dialogProps.open = dialogState === DIALOG_STATE.OPEN ? true : false;
    68	    }
    69	  }
    70	
    71	  return <BaseDialog {...dialogProps}>{children}</BaseDialog>;
    72	}

     1	import { Memoize, Unmemoize } from "@calcom/features/cache";
     2	import type { FeatureId } from "@calcom/features/flags/config";
     3	import type { FeatureDto } from "@calcom/lib/dto/FeatureDto";
     4	import { FeatureDtoArraySchema, FeatureDtoSchema } from "@calcom/lib/dto/FeatureDto";
     5	import type { IFeatureRepository } from "./PrismaFeatureRepository";
     6	
     7	const CACHE_PREFIX = "features:global";
     8	const KEY = {
     9	  all: (): string => `${CACHE_PREFIX}:all`,
    10	  bySlug: (slug: string): string => `${CACHE_PREFIX}:slug:${slug}`,
    11	};
    12	
    13	export class CachedFeatureRepository implements IFeatureRepository {
    14	  constructor(private prismaFeatureRepository: IFeatureRepository) {}
    15	
    16	  @Memoize({
    17	    key: KEY.all,
    18	    schema: FeatureDtoArraySchema,
    19	  })
    20	  async findAll(): Promise<FeatureDto[]> {
    21	    return this.prismaFeatureRepository.findAll();
    22	  }
    23	
    24	  @Memoize({
    25	    key: KEY.bySlug,
    26	    schema: FeatureDtoSchema.nullable(),
    27	  })
    28	  async findBySlug(slug: string): Promise<FeatureDto | null> {
    29	    return this.prismaFeatureRepository.findBySlug(slug);
    30	  }
    31	
    32	  @Unmemoize({
    33	    keys: (input: { featureId: FeatureId }) => [KEY.bySlug(input.featureId), KEY.all()],
    34	  })
    35	  async update(input: { featureId: FeatureId; enabled: boolean; updatedBy?: number }): Promise<FeatureDto> {
    36	    return this.prismaFeatureRepository.update(input);
    37	  }
    38	
    39	  /**
    40	   * Checks if a feature is enabled globally in the application.
    41	   * Uses the cached findBySlug method to avoid hitting the database on every request.
    42	   * @param slug - The feature flag identifier to check
    43	   * @returns Promise<boolean> - True if the feature is enabled globally, false otherwise
    44	   */
    45	  async checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally(slug: string): Promise<boolean> {
    46	    const feature = await this.findBySlug(slug);
    47	    return Boolean(feature && feature.enabled);
    48	  }
    49	
    50	  /**
    51	   * Gets a map of all feature flags and their enabled status.
    52	   * Uses caching to avoid hitting the database on every request.
    53	   * @returns Promise<AppFlags> - A map of feature flags to their enabled status
    54	   */
    55	  public async getFeatureFlagMap() {
    56	    const flags = await this.findAll();
    57	    return flags.reduce(
    58	      (acc, flag) => {
    59	        acc[flag.slug as FeatureId] = flag.enabled;
    60	        return acc;
    61	      },
    62	      {} as Record<string, boolean>
    63	    );
    64	  }
    65	}

<result>I traced the whole signup flow. Today nothing on the signup path or in the credentials login reads `REQUIRE_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH_FLAG`. The only places that use the flag or `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` are the admin security page, `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/security-view.tsx`, `FlagAdminList.tsx`, the config, and the helper and its test.

## 1. Signup UI
- **Page:** `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/signup/page.tsx`
- **View:** `/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx`. It's a client component, and there's a `signup-view.test.tsx` next to it.
- **Form schema (lines 56-59):** the API `signupSchema` from `packages/prisma/zod-utils.ts:849` (username optional, email, password, language, token), extended with `apiError` and `cfToken`. Lines 218-230 add a refinement that makes username required unless it's an org invite by link.
- **Fields:**
  - Username (lines 542-558): has a debounced availability and premium check through `fetchUsername`.
  - Email (561-570).
  - Password (573-580): hints are `caplow`, `min`, `num`.
  - Optional Cloudflare Turnstile (582-596).
  - Cookie-consent checkbox (598-602).
  - Submit button (611-625).
- **Email-form toggle:** the form only shows when `displayEmailForm` is true (it starts as `token`). Otherwise you get the Google, Microsoft and "continue with email" buttons (629-765).
- **Submit, `signUp` (270-376):** calls `fetchSignup({...data, language, token}, cfToken)`.
  - `fetchSignup` (`/Users/joshuako/Desktop/cal.diy/packages/features/auth/signup/lib/fetchSignup.ts:28-82`) POSTs JSON to `/api/auth/signup`, adds UTM params to the URL and sends a `cf-access-token` header.
  - It returns `{ok, data}` or `{ok:false, status, error}`. Helpers: `isUserAlreadyExistsError` (409), `hasCheckoutSession`, `isAccountUnderReview`.
- **After submit:**
  - 409 "user exists": shows a toast, then `router.push('/auth/login?callbackUrl=...')` after 3s (292-299).
  - Checkout session: Stripe redirect (301-310).
  - `accountUnderReview`: shows the under-review panel (315-318).
  - If `emailVerificationEnabled &amp;&amp; !token &amp;&amp; !isOrgInviteByLink`: saves username, email and password to `sessionStorage[SIGNUP_DRAFT_KEY]` (324-333).
  - Then it always signs in automatically with `signIn("credentials", {...data, callbackUrl})` (353-356). The callback is `${WEBAPP_URL}/auth/verify-email?from=signup` if email verification is on, otherwise `/getting-started` or `/onboarding/getting-started` (when `onboardingV3Enabled`). If a `callbackUrl` query param is present it wins (335-351).
  - Only email, password, username and language are passed to `signIn`. No `totpCode`.

## 2. Server handlers

- Confirmed: the return at `:504-526` starts with `...existingUserWithoutTeamsField, ...token,`. It then sets `profileId`, `upId`, `belongsToActiveTeam`, `orgAwareUsername` and `org`. Because `token` is spread second, its fields override the DB fields.
- This path runs whenever `user` is absent (`:528-530`), which means every token refresh after sign-in.

**Related facts that may matter:**
- **Credentials branch:** `inactiveAdminReason` is copied onto the token here (`:548-563`, at `:562`), and only at sign-in.
- **Session update trigger:** `trigger === "update"` (`:432-442`) returns `...token` plus `profileId`, `upId`, `locale`, `name`, `username` and `email` from the update payload.

- **Server-side sessions are built differently:** `packages/features/auth/lib/getServerSession.ts` builds its session from `prisma.user.findUnique` plus token fields (`session.user` at about `:101-125`). It uses `role: user.role` from the DB and leaves out `inactiveAdminReason`. So server components never see `INACTIVE_ADMIN` or that reason.

// Builds a node_modules "junction farm" inside the scratch clone so tests can run against the
// PR checkout without installing anything and without writing into the user's repo.
// Usage: node make-junctions.cjs <userRepo> <scratchClone>
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const [userRepo, scratch] = process.argv.slice(2).map((p) => path.resolve(p));
const SKIP_TOP = new Set([".vite", ".vite-temp", ".cache", ".vitest", "@calcom"]);
const NESTED = ["apps/web", "packages/lib", "packages/ui", "packages/trpc", "packages/prisma", "packages/platform/atoms"];

const junction = (target, linkPath) => fs.symlinkSync(target, linkPath, "junction");

const userNm = path.join(userRepo, "node_modules");
const scratchNm = path.join(scratch, "node_modules");
fs.mkdirSync(scratchNm, { recursive: true });

let made = 0;
for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(userNm, { withFileTypes: true })) {
  if (SKIP_TOP.has(entry.name)) continue;
  const src = path.join(userNm, entry.name);
  const dst = path.join(scratchNm, entry.name);
  if (fs.existsSync(dst)) continue;
  if (fs.statSync(src).isDirectory()) {
    junction(src, dst);
    made++;
  }
}

// Workspace packages must resolve to the PR checkout, not the user's working tree
const calcomDst = path.join(scratchNm, "@calcom");
fs.mkdirSync(calcomDst, { recursive: true });
const userPrefix = userRepo.toLowerCase();
let rewired = 0;
let fallback = 0;
for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(path.join(userNm, "@calcom"))) {
  const real = fs.realpathSync(path.join(userNm, "@calcom", entry));
  let target = real;
  if (real.toLowerCase().startsWith(userPrefix)) {
    const candidate = path.join(scratch, real.slice(userRepo.length));
    if (fs.existsSync(candidate)) {
      target = candidate;
      rewired++;
    } else {
      fallback++;
    }
  }
  junction(target, path.join(calcomDst, entry));
}

for (const rel of NESTED) {
  const src = path.join(userRepo, rel, "node_modules");
  const dst = path.join(scratch, rel, "node_modules");
  if (fs.existsSync(src) && !fs.existsSync(dst)) junction(src, dst);
}

console.log(JSON.stringify({ topLevelJunctions: made, calcomRewired: rewired, calcomFallback: fallback }));

```

```cjs
// Re-points scratch node_modules/@calcom links: packages the PR changes resolve to the scratch
// checkout; every other workspace package resolves to the user's installed copy, which carries
// generated files (e.g. @calcom/prisma/enums) that a bare checkout lacks.
// Usage: node repoint-calcom.cjs <userRepo> <scratchClone>
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const [userRepo, scratch] = process.argv.slice(2).map((p) => path.resolve(p));
const PR_CHANGED_DIRS = ["packages/features", "apps/web", "packages/i18n", "packages/types"].map((d) =>
  path.join(userRepo, d).toLowerCase()
);

const userCalcom = path.join(userRepo, "node_modules", "@calcom");
const scratchCalcom = path.join(scratch, "node_modules", "@calcom");

const summary = { toScratch: [], toUser: 0 };
for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(scratchCalcom)) {
  const link = path.join(scratchCalcom, entry);
  if (!fs.lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Refusing to touch non-link ${link}`);
  // Non-recursive rmdir removes only the junction itself, never the target's contents
  fs.rmdirSync(link);

  const userReal = fs.realpathSync(path.join(userCalcom, entry));
  const isChanged = PR_CHANGED_DIRS.includes(userReal.toLowerCase());
  const target = isChanged ? path.join(scratch, userReal.slice(userRepo.length)) : userReal;
  fs.symlinkSync(target, link, "junction");
  if (isChanged) summary.toScratch.push(entry);
  else summary.toUser++;
}
console.log(JSON.stringify(summary));

```

const TwoFactorAuthAPI = {
  async setup(password: string) {
    return fetch("/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup", {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({ password }),
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
    });
  },

  async enable(code: string) {
    return fetch("/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable", {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({ code }),
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
    });
  },

  async disable(password: string, code: string, backupCode: string) {
    return fetch("/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable", {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({ password, code, backupCode }),
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
    });
  },
};

const passwordInput = () => screen.getByRole("dialog").querySelector('input[name="password"]') as HTMLInputElement;
const pressEscape = () => fireEvent.keyDown(screen.getByRole("dialog"), { key: "Escape" });

describe("review probe: real EnableTwoFactorModal", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    mocks.sessionUser = { requiresTwoFactorSetup: true, role: "USER" };

  });

    expect(screen.queryByText("cancel")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    pressEscape();
    expect(screen.getByRole("dialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("flash: after Continue on the backup codes, the password step re-renders until update() resolves", async () => {
    mocks.setup.mockResolvedValue({
      status: 200,
      json: async () => ({ backupCodes: ["aaaaabbbbb"], dataUri: "data:,", secret: "SECRET", keyUri: "k" }),
    });
    mocks.enable.mockResolvedValue({ status: 200, json: async () => ({}) });
    let resolveUpdate: (v: null) => void = () => {};

    expect(screen.getByTestId("2fa-required-notice")).toBeInTheDocument();

// Removes every junction/symlink inside the scratch clone without ever recursing into one,
// so nothing in the user's repo or node_modules can be touched.
// Usage: node remove-junctions.cjs <scratchClone>
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
let removed = 0;
let scannedDirs = 0;

const walk = (dir) => {
  scannedDirs++;
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
    const p = path.join(dir, entry);
    const st = fs.lstatSync(p);
    if (st.isSymbolicLink()) {
      // Non-recursive: removes only the link itself
      fs.rmdirSync(p);
      removed++;
    } else if (st.isDirectory() && entry !== ".git") {
      walk(p);
    }
  }
};

walk(root);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ removedLinks: removed, scannedDirs }));

```

I reviewed PR #120 at its head commit `4ef4fb3`. My recommendation is **Request Changes**. The server-side design is solid, but there's one confirmed bug where the required 2FA modal can't be closed or finished, and the PR's tests never exercise the "can't be closed" behavior. Nothing was posted to GitHub, and your branch, working tree and `node_modules` are unchanged.

## Section A — Detailed findings (for you)

**What I inspected and ran**
- The PR description, issue #112 (6 acceptance criteria plus Out of Scope), and the full diff at `4ef4fb3`.
- The existing code the diff depends on: the NextAuth callbacks, the custom `getServerSession`, the dialog components, `Shell`, the onboarding flow and its `onboarding-v3` gate, the flag cache, the TOTP setup route, and `UserRepository.findById`.
- **Tests, run by me in a separate clone:** the PR's 6 test files plus 8 related existing ones. **14 files, 113 tests passed.**
- **CI:** it also ran all 6 new test files, and Unit tests, Type Checks and Lint pass. The failing Security Audit is third-party advisories: it also failed on the already-merged #113, and this PR changes no dependencies.
- **Extra tests I wrote** (in the scratch clone only): 4 probe tests against the real modal, and 1 mutation test where I deliberately broke the modal to see whether the PR's tests notice.
- The AI log (12 human prompts across 19 turns) and the PR's screenshot.

**Acceptance criteria**

| AC | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Server decides at login; 3 conditions; browser can't skip | Met | `next-auth-options.ts:269-272`; the `update` branch re-reads the DB and ignores the client's payload (`:447-450`, tested) |
| 2. Unclosable setup window on every page | Met in the UI, but untested and has a dead end | `Shell.tsx:44`, `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:182,242`; my probe confirms there's no Cancel and Escape is ignored |
| 3. User can use the app normally after setup | Met (admins are signed out on purpose) | `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx:23-31` |
| 4. Onboarding 2FA step | Met in the new onboarding flow, which is on globally | `useFinishPersonalOnboarding.ts`, `two-factor/page.tsx` |
| 5. Google/other identity-provider users exempt | Met | `requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts:10`; tests for GOOGLE, SAML, AZUREAD |
| 6. Tests for the login rule and onboarding step | Partial | Both are tested; the modal's AC2 behavior is not |
| Out of scope: already-logged-in users wait until next login | Deviates | `next-auth-options.ts:524` recalculates the flag on every session fetch |

**Findings, most severe first**

1. **The modal can get stuck where it can't be closed or finished.** Medium, confirmed bug.
   - **Where:** `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx:15-21`, `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:122-126`, `totp/setup/route.ts:53-55`.
   - **What happens:** once the modal opens, its `open` state never goes back to closed.
     - With two tabs open, finishing setup in tab A clears the flag when tab B is focused (next-auth refetches the session on focus by default).
     - Tab B's modal stays on the password step anyway.
     - Submitting there returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`, which shows as "something went wrong". There's no Cancel and Escape is ignored, so only a reload gets out.
     - The same happens if an admin turns the setting off while a user has the modal open.
   - **Evidence:** my probe test reproduces it with the real modal. The PR's own test at `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.test.tsx:61` asserts this behavior. The agent's manual test plan in the AI log (around line 14165) expected the opposite: "Window B's popup disappears on focus. It isn't stuck."
   - **Fix:** keep the modal open only after 2FA was enabled *in this modal*. For example, add an `onEnabled` callback that fires when `TwoFactorAuthAPI.enable` succeeds, and use `open = isRequired || enabledHere`. Also consider a "Sign out" link in required mode: AC2 forbids Cancel/Close, but sign-out gives an exit when setup fails for other reasons (no password on the account, rate limiting, server error).

2. **The core "can't be closed" behavior (AC2) has no real test.** Medium, confirmed gap.
   - **Where:** both component tests mock out `EnableTwoFactorModal` entirely. `vitest.config.mts:58` has no `@components/*` alias, so the real modal can't even load in tests.
   - **Evidence:** I changed `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:242` and `:189` so that required mode shows a Cancel button and drops the notice. All 6 PR test files (64 tests) still passed. A test against the real modal caught it immediately.
   - **Fix:** add the alias to the vitest config (mirroring `apps/web/tsconfig.json`) and wrap renders in `TooltipProvider`. Then assert: the notice shows, there's no Cancel, Escape doesn't close it, and the backup-codes button says "Continue". Also test that Continue/Skip in `PersonalCalendarView` routes to the 2FA step; only the hook behind it is tested now.

3. **Enforcement is UI-only, but the PR text says otherwise.** Medium. This is a limitation, not an AC failure.
   - **Where:** the custom `getServerSession.ts:101-125` never runs the token callback and doesn't carry the flag. Completing onboarding is a client-side `updateProfile({ completedOnboarding: true })` call (`useSubmitPersonalOnboarding.ts:88-93`).
   - **Why it matters:** nothing on the server blocks tRPC/API calls while setup is required. Someone could remove the dialog in devtools and keep using the app.
   - **Overclaims to correct:** the PR description's "inescapable site-wide enforcement" and "e.g., `getServerSession`" recalculation claim, and the comment at `useFinishPersonalOnboarding.ts:17` ("can't be finished without 2FA"). The PR's own `page.tsx:35` comment contradicts the `getServerSession` claim.
   - **Fix:** reword those, and open a follow-up issue for server-side blocking of regular users. #67 only covers admins.

4. **Already-logged-in users are forced immediately.** This needs your decision as the issue author.
   - **Where:** `next-auth-options.ts:524` recalculates the flag on every session fetch.
   - **Why it matters:** #112's Out of Scope says the rule applies at the user's next login. With this PR, logged-in users get the modal on their next session refetch, such as when they focus the window. That's arguably better, and the PR explains it as its "Option C", but it changes the agreed scope without saying so relative to the issue.
   - **Fix:** accept it and update the issue, or ask the author to align with the spec.

5. **The password step flashes back after clicking Continue.** Low, confirmed bug.
   - **Where:** `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:288-289` resets to the password step before calling `onEnable()`. `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx:29-30` only closes after `await update()`.
   - **Evidence:** my probe shows the password field and the "administrator requires" notice rendered again while the session refresh is pending.
   - **Fix:** close the modal first, as `personal-two-factor-view.tsx:25` already does.

6. **Every session `update()` now loads far more than it needs.** Low.
   - **Where:** `next-auth-options.ts:437-438` and `page.tsx:29` call `findById`, whose select list (`UserRepository.ts:83-122`) includes `twoFactorSecret`, `backupCodes`, `teams` and `profiles`.
   - **Why it matters:** the `update` branch made no database call before. Now every `update()` (9 places call it) loads encrypted 2FA data and related records just to compute one true/false value. The repo's rules say to select only the fields you need.
   - **Fix:** add a narrow repository method that returns only `twoFactorEnabled` and `identityProvider`.

7. **Two different ways to read the same setting.** Low.
   - **Where:** `requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts:13` reads the flag through the cached repository. #111's `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide.ts:5` reads it straight from the database.
   - **Why it matters:** it's not a bug today, because I verified that toggling the setting clears the cache entry. But two helpers for one rule will drift apart.
   - **Fix:** keep a single helper.

8. **`EnableTwoFactorModal`'s props got looser for every caller.** Low.
   - **Where:** `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:20,25` make `onOpenChange` and `onCancel` optional.
   - **Why it matters:** a future normal (non-required) caller that forgets them silently gets a dialog that can't be dismissed, with a Cancel button that does nothing.
   - **Fix:** a discriminated union type, so the handlers are required unless `isRequired` is true.

9. **Onboarding could bounce on a stale session.** Low, possible but not reproduced.
   - **Where:** the hook decides from the browser's session copy (`useFinishPersonalOnboarding.ts:14-19`), but the 2FA step page decides from the database (`page.tsx:36-37`).
   - **Why it matters:** if they disagree (for example, setup was finished in another tab), clicking Continue goes to the 2FA step, gets redirected back to the calendar step, and repeats until the session refetches.

10. **Process issues.** Low.
    - `docs/sprint2/diagrams/111-kojoshuay.md` is a #111 change; in the AI log, the agent explicitly said to leave it out.
    - The PR has 18 code files and about 790 changed lines, over the repo's guideline of under 10 files and 500 lines.
    - The commit message isn't in conventional-commit format, and the PR title isn't descriptive.

**Checked and ruled out**

- The new onboarding flow being off: it's enabled globally by migration `20260213000000`. The old `/getting-started` flow has no 2FA step, but those users still get the global modal.

- Regressions to the existing settings-page 2FA modal: my probe confirms Cancel still shows and Escape still closes it.
- Secrets in the 687 KB AI log: none found.

## Findings (PR-head line numbers)
1. **Medium, confirmed bug: stuck, undismissable modal.**

   - Scenario: two tabs; finish setup in tab A; tab B refetches on focus and the flag goes false, but its modal stays on the password step. Submitting returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` (`apps/web/app/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup/route.ts:53-55`). `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:122-126` shows any non-IncorrectPassword error as "something_went_wrong". There's no Cancel and Escape is ignored, so only a reload gets out. The same happens if an admin turns the setting off.
   - The PR's test at `__tests__/RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.test.tsx:61` asserts this latch. The agent's manual test plan (AI log, about line 14165, row 4) expected "Window B's popup disappears on focus. It isn't stuck."
   - Fix: latch only after 2FA is enabled in this modal (an `onEnabled` callback; `open = isRequired || enabledHere`, or a phase state). Optionally add a "Sign out" link in required mode as an exit for any setup error (UserMissingPassword, 429, missing encryption key 500).
2. **Medium, confirmed test gap.** No test covers AC2. Both component tests mock `EnableTwoFactorModal`, and `vitest.config.mts:58` has no `@components` alias, so the real modal can't load in tests (the mutation result above proves the gap). The `PersonalCalendarView` Continue/Skip routing and the settings `totalSteps` wiring are also untested. Fix: add the alias (mirroring `apps/web/tsconfig.json`) plus a `TooltipProvider` wrapper and real-modal tests.
3. **Medium limitation (not an AC violation): enforcement is UI-only.**
   - Custom `packages/features/auth/lib/getServerSession.ts:101-125` never runs the jwt callback and has no flag.
   - Onboarding completion is a client call, `viewer.me.updateProfile({ completedOnboarding: true })` (`apps/web/modules/onboarding/hooks/useSubmitPersonalOnboarding.ts:88-93`).

   - Fix: reword, and open a follow-up issue for server-side gating of regular users (#67 covers admins only).
4. **Decision for the issue author: scope deviation.** `next-auth-options.ts:524` recomputes the flag in `autoMergeIdentities` on every session fetch, so already-logged-in users are forced immediately even though the issue put that out of scope.
5. **Low, confirmed bug: password-step flash.** `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:288-289` calls `resetState()` before `onEnable()`, and `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal.tsx:29-30` only closes after `await update()`. Fix: close first, as `personal-two-factor-view.tsx:25` already does.

The update branch previously made no DB call, and there are 9 `update()` call sites. Fix: a narrow select.
7. **Low: duplicate flag read.** `requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts:13` reads the flag through the cached repo; #111's `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide.ts:5` reads it through the uncached Prisma repo. Cache invalidation on toggle is correct (`CachedFeatureRepository.ts:32-37` via `toggleFeatureFlag.handler.ts:17-22`; Redis with a 5-minute TTL), so this isn't a bug, just two helpers for one rule.
8. **Low: looser props.** `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:20,25` makes `onOpenChange` and `onCancel` optional for every caller. Suggest a discriminated union.
